races.name: British Stallion Studs 'Carrie Red' EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Angel Sense
runners_data.note: Won on standard going and has placed on soft-equivalent surfaces; prominent runner for Marco Botti and Marco Ghiani who should sit just off the three leaders and use her 6f/soft experience well over this 6½f trip.

runners_data.name: Kodi Bear Light
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's yard is in excellent form (12/40 in 14 days) and Jack Nicholls takes the 3lb claim; this hold-up filly won over 7f on good last time and a strongly-run 6½f on soft ground suits her patient style perfectly.

runners_data.name: Downonmainstreet
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back on good ground and ran just 14 days ago for Michael Bell, suggesting the team is happy with her; prominent runner who should find a natural position just behind the three pace-setters, but the step onto soft ground is an unproven factor.

runners_data.name: Roosike
runners_data.note: One of three confirmed front-runners, she has won on standard ground and placed on similar going but her last run over 7f soft saw her finish 14th — her stamina for a gruelling 6½f on today's surface needs scrutiny.

runners_data.name: Rollthedicebaby
runners_data.note: Hannon's filly is a genuine front-runner by nature but cannot get to the front in a race that already has three confirmed leaders, placing her in unaccustomed midfield territory; her soft-ground record is 2/5 which is encouraging, but racing against the grain of her natural style is a clear negative.

runners_data.name: Leucothea
runners_data.note: Third front-runner in the race and the lowest-rated of the trio at OR 73; her record on soft-equivalent going reads 0W1P from six attempts, and with two rivals equally keen to lead, she may be outpaced by her own front-running companions.

runners_data.name: Wondervision
runners_data.note: Three-race maiden winner for Jack Channon who is naturally prominent but will be squeezed out of position by the three genuine leaders; her form has been on standard ground and she has never encountered soft, adding a second layer of uncertainty to her effectiveness here.

runners_data.name: Angel In My Heart
runners_data.note: Won on good ground and placed on standard going for Adrian Keatley's small team (0/10 in 14 days), and though she prefers to race up with the pace, she will be denied that position by the front-running trio — Luke Morris will need to adapt her tactics.

runners_data.name: Bayside
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Rod Millman who won on soft-equivalent going and has recent form over 7f on soft/standard; her natural off-the-pace style is ideally placed to exploit a strongly-run race, and Cam Hardie rides with experience of her style.

runners_data.name: Sexy Chick
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR 93 and 135lbs in the hands of Oisin Murphy for Richard Spencer; ran fifth on soft last time out and her best form has come on good ground, so the ground is a mild concern despite Murphy's ability to compensate tactically.

runners_data.name: Art Of Life
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners this Clive Cox-trained filly who has finished second in both recent starts on good ground; she is one of three front-runners and likely to face a fierce duel for the lead from the off, which may undermine her finishing reserves on soft ground.

runners_data.name: Bymiddaytomorrow
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly won her last two starts over 7f on good ground and Ashley Lewis claims 3lbs; her record on soft-equivalent ground reads 0W0P from two runs but she is progressive and the step up to 6½f — closer to her winning trip of 7f — is a genuine asset.

runners_data.name: Speed of Sound
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer also runs Sexy Chick and Saffie Osborne takes the ride on this prominent filly who won over 6f on good and placed on soft; an honest consistent profile with three places from four runs, and she should travel comfortably in the prominent group just behind the leaders.

races.paceDynamic: Art Of Life, Roosike, and Leucothea are three confirmed front-runners in a 13-runner field, and with all three likely to contest the lead from the off on good-to-soft ground at Doncaster, a strong, contested gallop is virtually guaranteed from the first stride. That sustained early pressure over 6½f on soft-leaning ground will stretch the field significantly and drain the finishing reserves of those who try to match the pace setters, making this a genuine stamina examination for every runner. The field holds more prominent-speed types than the race shape can physically accommodate — Rollthedicebaby, Wondervision, and Angel In My Heart are all natural prominent racers who are likely to be shuffled back by the three genuine leaders and will find themselves in unfamiliar midfield territory, reducing their effectiveness. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and patient-travelling horses who can sit off a genuine tempo, conserve energy through the middle of the race, and produce a sustained late run — closers and off-the-pace finishers are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Stamina Settles
scenarios.trigger: If Art Of Life, Roosike, and Leucothea tear into the lead and collectively set a punishing pace that burns out the front rank.
scenarios.body: The three leaders scorch through the first half of the race, and as the ground takes its toll in the final two furlongs the field strings out; horses who have been settled in the early stages arrive with the most momentum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners reach a tacit equilibrium and the pace proves steadier than expected for the first three furlongs.
scenarios.body: One of Art Of Life or Roosike gains a comfortable lead without being truly pressured, conserving enough to hold on; prominent types who travel sweetly close to the pace then become dangers rather than victims.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a strong but not suicidal pace and one of the well-positioned prominent types survives in the slipstream.
scenarios.body: Angel Sense or Speed of Sound, travelling fluently just off the pace, inherit a winning position without ever being exposed to the full brunt of the early tempo; both have the form in soft-leaning going to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Reach
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly extreme and the race collapses into chaos, leaving a gap for a well-handicapped runner with a big last-time-out effort.
scenarios.body: Bymiddaytomorrow, who won twice over 7f on good and has strong recent form, or Sexy Chick stepping back from a wide margin win, make late ground but the hot pace stretches the field too wide for closers to truly close.

watchPoints.text: Art Of Life, Roosike, and Leucothea are all confirmed front-runners — watch for a fierce three-way battle for the lead from the gates that could produce a suicidal pace, burning each other out and dramatically opening the race to hold-up horses.

Rollthedicebaby, Wondervision, and Angel In My Heart are all natural prominent racers who cannot get their preferred positions — watch whether their jockeys attempt to force the issue early and cause interference or whether they accept midfield roles and ride against type.

Leucothea is the lowest-rated front-runner (OR 73) and her soft-ground record is 0W1P from six attempts — watch whether she is allowed to stride clear early or whether she is immediately under pressure from Art Of Life and Roosike and weakens before halfway.

Bymiddaytomorrow is stepping down from 7f to 6½f but that trip is closer to her proven winning distance than the 6f runs in her career — watch whether Ashley Lewis uses the 3lb claim to position her close enough to challenge over the final furlong on soft ground.

Kodi Bear Light won over 7f last time and the hold-up style of K.R. Burke's yard suits a strongly-run race; watch whether Jack Nicholls (3lb claim) gives her a clean run from the rear as the field strings out in the final two furlongs.

races.name: Weatherbys £300,000 2-Y-O Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Mithaaly
runners_data.note: Placed in all three starts including twice at 7f+, Buick booking for Boughey is a strong positive, and prominent style suits a race where the pace is fast but she need not be part of the early battle.

runners_data.name: Ongombo
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Charlie Fellowes who has finished placed on Good ground; the big-field soft-ground scenario could help but past Stratford runs suggest limited improvement available.

runners_data.name: Satellite Of Love
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good ground and has soft form (5th last time), Clive Cox's runner wants to lead but faces severe competition for that role; her 1W in 3 soft-ground runs is encouraging but the contested pace could find her out.

runners_data.name: Stardom Glory
runners_data.note: James Doyle's mount for Hugo Palmer wants to go toe-to-toe for the lead from stall, has won over 6f on Good and placed multiple times at this trip, but finished 6th on a step up to 7f on Good — suspect the hot pace here on soft ground may stop her late.

runners_data.name: The Dancing Pirate
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Balding on a horse who has been prominent without winning at 5f and 6f, consistent form string of 44273 suggests a reliable but hard-to-win type; prominently placed but needs those in front to tire sharply.

runners_data.name: Dorigo
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott partners the Kevin Ryan-trained colt who finished 4th on soft ground at 5f and 2nd twice on Good at 6f; the soft going is a known quantity with a near-miss on similar, and a prominent stalking role suits if the pace is as fierce as expected.

runners_data.name: A Bear Affair
runners_data.note: Sean Levey rides for Richard Hannon; headgear (b) fitted, soft-ground experience with one win from seven on similar going, runs from behind and has the profile of a horse who needs something to go wrong upfront — this race may provide exactly that.

runners_data.name: Secret Society
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's second string wants the lead but has finished 7th and 6th in her two soft-ground starts, so her going record is a concern; likely to be pushed off the pace by stronger rivals, reducing her effectiveness significantly.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Glory
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has won on Firm and placed on Firm at 6f, but has finished 11th twice on Good and 4th on Good — course form is inconsistent and soft ground appears untested; going to struggle to secure the lead with Night In Vegas and Stardom Glory present.

runners_data.name: Night In Vegas
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR=102, one soft-ground win from five runs on similar going, and has won twice at 6f; the class advantage is real but Bishop must deal with multiple pace rivals and 6½f on soft is a stamina test for an early-speed type.

runners_data.name: Seven Nation Army
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's hold-up runner has won over 7f on soft, placed twice at 8f, and has form over 6f on soft — the step up from sprint to middle-distance form is encouraging for a soft-ground 6½f, and David Probert can hunt the pace from the rear.

runners_data.name: Zigazig Ah
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne partners Richard Spencer's filly who has won at 5f and 6f on Good and placed at 6f on Slow; a prominent racer with consistent form in the right races, but stepping up slightly on class here.

runners_data.name: Alfa Hoodini
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani rides Ivan Furtado's lightly raced runner with just one run (7th at Stratford on Standard); an OR of 120 appears to be a notional entry-level mark and no genuine evidence this horse can compete at this level.

runners_data.name: Backmeifyoucan
runners_data.note: Luke Morris takes the mount for Furtado; two runs both poor at Stratford on Standard going, and the unknown style flag plus lightly-raced tag make this an impossible runner to assess with any confidence at this level.

runners_data.name: Blazing Inferno
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope's pick for Edward Bethell is unbeaten in one run (1st at 6f on Good), a promising profile but single-run horses must be treated with caution in a 17-runner field; prominent racer who will need to step sharply forward.

runners_data.name: God Given Talent
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand for William Haggas, the headgear (t) addition is notable — blinkers-free conversion often shows improved focus; won over 6f on Good on debut but followed with a distant 19th suggesting inconsistency; prominent type who could improve dramatically.

runners_data.name: Icy Moon
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves rides the third Furtado runner; one start (6th at Stratford on Standard) offers nothing to work with, an OR of 120 is a nominal figure, and unknown style makes race integration entirely speculative.

races.paceDynamic: Night In Vegas (OR=102, the class horse of the field), Satellite Of Love, Stardom Glory, Secret Society, and Sovereign Glory all want to lead, guaranteeing a strong, contested pace from the outset over 6½f on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster. With five confirmed front-runners scrapping for position early, the pace is likely to be genuinely strong from the off, and on softening turf that will stretch stamina reserves significantly in the final two furlongs. The leaders will be unable to all get their positions — Night In Vegas and Stardom Glory carry the class and connections to boss the rail, while Secret Society and Sovereign Glory are likely to be shuffled back from their natural roles under pressure. This contested, honest gallop set by multiple pace-setters on soft ground strongly favours hold-up and come-from-behind horses who can travel through the field and pick off tired leaders late, with prominent types who travel kindly at a strong pace also in play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners set a genuinely fierce gallop that stretches the field, allowing hold-up horses to pick them off in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The contested pace burns out the leaders rounding into the straight, leaving the last two furlongs a test of raw stamina on soft ground, perfectly suited to horses held up to conserve energy. Seven Nation Army, who has won on soft and over further, and A Bear Affair, who has soft-ground form, are positioned to sweep through in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Horse Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Night In Vegas breaks sharply and secures a measured lead, controlling the tempo rather than burning out in a pace duel.
scenarios.body: Night In Vegas is the highest-rated runner at OR=102 with a win on soft ground already in the book, and with Charles Bishop able to find a position on the rail she could dictate without fully blowing herself up despite the presence of other speed horses. If she gets away cleanly at a controlled tempo she has the class to hold on as rivals tire around her in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but a prominently-placed horse tracks the leaders just off the pace and pounces inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mithaaly for William Buick and George Boughey has been placed twice at 7f on Good ground and is proven at this trip, allowing her to travel handily just off the hot pace without expending early energy; Dorigo and God Given Talent profile similarly as tracked stalkers. The soft ground tests those who led throughout while these types, sitting two lengths off the lead, find another gear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong as all leaders tie up simultaneously on soft ground, triggering a dramatic late swoop from the back.
scenarios.body: Alfa Hoodini and Backmeifyoucan are lightly raced unknowns from Ivan Furtado's yard who, if they have ability to match their high entry-level OR, could benefit from finding a clear run late as the field bunches. This scenario requires chaos upfront and is the least predictable shape, dependent on horses with limited exposed form hitting their ceiling at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Night In Vegas and Stardom Glory both want to lead — watch the first two furlongs for a battle for the rail that could burn both out before halfway and dramatically alter the race shape.

Sovereign Glory and Secret Society are confirmed front-runners who are likely to be shuffled off the pace by higher-class speedsters; if they drop back into midfield involuntarily, they become largely irrelevant to the outcome.

Seven Nation Army's soft-ground win at 7f on Soft makes him a key danger if the pace collapses in the final furlong — David Probert will be tracking the field for a late sweep and this scenario is underappreciated.
Blazing Inferno is a one-run winner for Bethell with Tudhope booked — watch if he travels easily in the prominent group, as unexposed horses from this yard have shown rapid improvement before.
God Given Talent carries the Haggas/Marquand combination and the tongue-tie addition; a big performance from a yard known for placing horses correctly — monitor market moves before the off.

races.name: Pertemps Network Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Runman
runners_data.note: Won his last two starts on Good ground over a mile, now stepping up to 1m2f on soft for John & Thady Gosden and Oisin Murphy — the trip is the key question, but pedigree and trainer profile suggest he handles the extra furlong; sits naturally prominent and should find the perfect stalking berth behind Spyce.

runners_data.name: King Of Earth
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old has won twice including at nine furlongs on good-soft, so the combination of trip and going looks squarely in his favour; Tom Marquand rides and he is naturally prominent, having finished second on his only soft-ground start — solid each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Knights Charge
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's colt won his last two starts including over 1m2f on soft, making the combination of form, trip, and going compelling; he is a true prominent racer by nature but with five declared prominently-inclined rivals, he is likely to find himself slightly further back than ideal — a structural discount applies but raw form is strong.

runners_data.name: Wild Thoughts
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's filly has won and placed prominently before but her last five starts on good ground suggest soft is unproven territory; naturally keen and forward-going, she will want to race up with the pace but is one of several types squeezed out of that position — her chance is compromised as much by race shape as by the ground.

runners_data.name: Bourbon Blues
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount on Brian Meehan's three-year-old who has placed twice at 1m2f on soft — a genuine hold-up horse who needs a proper gallop to make his ground-eating late run count; soft ground helps him conserve energy but a controlled pace set by Spyce makes his task harder.

runners_data.name: Spyce
runners_data.note: Alan King's colt is the confirmed lone front-runner and won over a mile on soft last time in his career — this is his race to control; his [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects that the solo-leader role may stretch his finishing kick if pursuers come at him fresh, but the tactical advantage of uncontested lead is real.

runners_data.name: Besieged
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's lightly-raced three-year-old won last time on soft over 1m2f and shaped with promise throughout — a 93-day break is the main query but the form is directly applicable; naturally prominent and with only three career starts, there may be further improvement to come at this trip and going combination.

runners_data.name: Strength Of Spirit
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's sprightly performer has won on good and shown form at around nine furlongs, but his natural urge to be close to the pace will be frustrated here — pushed further back than he likes, he is racing outside his comfort zone, and soft ground at this trip adds further questions to his profile.

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Donny
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's progressive three-year-old won his last start on soft over 1m2f and has a strong record at this trip and going combination (2W3P from 10 soft-ground runs); just four days since his last run is the only reservation — Duran Fentiman keeps the ride and his hold-up style suits a race that could get testing late.

runners_data.name: Sintra
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly won at 1m2f on good ground and has placed prominently before, but 117 days off the track and the shift to soft is an unknown; she wants to race prominently by nature but with so many similar types in the field, Nicola Currie will have to decide early whether to push forward or settle — either way it compromises her.

runners_data.name: Darius Dark
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's hold-up specialist has a remarkable record over longer trips — three wins from 12 furlongs on good — but soft ground is only 1W1P from eight attempts, and the drop back from 13f to 1m2f is a big ask; Luke Morris will deploy him from the rear but he needs genuine pace to reel in.

races.paceDynamic: Spyce is the confirmed pace-setter and will go forward from the outset, likely uncontested on the front end over this 1m2f on Good To Soft ground at Doncaster, creating a sustainable, controlled tempo rather than a truly searching gallop. Runman and King Of Earth are the natural prominent companions who should slot in directly behind Spyce, giving the front rank a degree of cover without generating any real pressure on the leader. The field contains a glut of horses whose true style is prominent — Knights Charge, Wild Thoughts, Strength Of Spirit, Sintra, and Besieged all want to race near the pace but cannot all do so, meaning several will be forced to settle further back than ideal and race out of their natural role. With a lone front-runner dictating a measured tempo on soft-leaning ground, horses racing prominently in the first two or three immediately behind Spyce hold a clear structural advantage, while genuine hold-up types face a stern test of finishing speed if the pace is not truly end-to-end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Spyce Dictates Controlled Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Spyce goes unchallenged and sets a measured, uncontested pace that suits horses racing in the first three.
scenarios.body: Spyce leads at his own rhythm on Good To Soft ground, and the horses immediately behind him — Runman and King Of Earth — race in the ideal stalking positions with a clear view of the leader; when the tempo lifts from two furlongs out, those within striking distance have the energy reserves to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely contested and produces a strong enough gallop to leave the prominent horses vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A busier-than-expected early pace exhausts those who have raced prominently throughout, opening the door for the true hold-up runners who have been biding their time at the rear; Bourbon Blues or Stoneacre Donny, both proven on soft ground, would be best placed to mow them down from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Spyce's uncontested lead translates into a wire-to-wire victory as the field fails to close on softening ground.
scenarios.body: Soft ground rewards a horse who can conserve energy by leading without pressure, and Spyce — who has won on soft before — may simply not be caught if the field is slow to organise its challenge; horses who have been redistributed rearward are least likely to get competitive runs from their unnatural positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If the over-supply of prominent types jostles for position in the early stages, producing an erratic tempo that unsettles the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Horses like Wild Thoughts, Knights Charge, and Sintra — all natural prominent types squeezed out of position — may push forward aggressively and disrupt the intended order, creating a ragged pace that randomises the result; in such a scenario lightly-raced improvers with tactical adaptability benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Spyce (Rossa Ryan) — if he walks the field up early and secures a completely uncontested lead, the race could be over a long way from home; watch whether Runman or King Of Earth's riders push up to apply even token pressure.

Knights Charge — 114 days off the track returning on soft ground for Roger Varian; a yard with a strong record but the fitness question is real, and if he is not spot-on after this layoff his strong form figures may flatter his chance today.

Wild Thoughts and Strength Of Spirit — both genuine front-runners who may push forward aggressively in the opening furlong despite being mapped to midfield; any early barging for position could unsettle the pace and compromise their own runs.

Stoneacre Donny — raced just four days ago; watch the market for signs the Easterby yard is confident he has bounced out of his last run in good shape, as soft ground and 1m2f are demonstrably his conditions.

Bourbon Blues (Ryan Moore) — if the race is truly run to suit hold-up horses and the tape shows Moore tracking closer than expected in the early stages, he may be reading something that the pace map does not fully capture; his soft-ground form at 1m2f is the relevant qualifier.

races.name: Betfred Park Hill Fillies' Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Consent
runners_data.note: A 4yo prominent runner with solid soft-ground credentials (5/8 starts on sim-going), wearing headgear, trained by Prescott who excels placing horses to peak at the right moment; the 40-day break is typical of Prescott's patient approach and she should be near peak fitness, well-suited to tracking a lone front-runner from close range.|

runners_data.name: Danielle
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride for Gosden, and this 5yo has two wins from six starts on similar going including a course-and-distance type win, travelling prominently — the combination of elite jockeyship, proven stamina, and soft-ground form makes her a natural fit for this controlled-pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: Fairy Glen
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will get an uncontested lead, but the 112-day layoff is substantial and she is flagged as racing out of role (STYLE_FIT 0.91) — expect her to control the race but treat her win chance cautiously given fitness queries and a soft-ground record that includes a fifth in heavy-ish conditions at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Floresta
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up filly by profile whose best form includes a win at 1m4f on soft and a second at the same trip, though she has not gone beyond that distance; Ben Coen rides and J P Murtagh has her ready after a 53-day break, but the uncontested pace may simply not be searching enough to bring her home past prominent trackers.|

runners_data.name: Nyra
runners_data.note: Strong form at 1m2f and 1m4f with two places on similar going, but her natural prominent style has been pushed to midfield here because the forward positions are oversubscribed — if she cannot access her natural position, her 0W record suggests she needs everything to fall right, and STYLE_FIT (0.90) underlines the positional risk.|

runners_data.name: Ryka
runners_data.note: Won on soft ground at 1m2f but her two most recent runs produced 8th and 6th-place finishes, and 1m6½f is a trip extension she has not proven; her prominent instincts are displaced to midfield by the race shape, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects that she is unlikely to get the race run to suit her natural forward-tracking style.|

runners_data.name: Waardah
runners_data.note: Three wins from eight starts on similar going, including at 1m4f on soft, and a second at 1m4f on Good to Soft — Callum Rodriguez rides and she wears headgear (hg:h) which has coincided with her best form; her prominent style fits the race shape perfectly and her soft-ground record is the strongest in the field.|

runners_data.name: Cameo
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride on this 3yo, who carries a 9lb age allowance, but her recent form is inconsistent (515386) and her true front-side tendencies cannot be expressed from the midfield position the race shape forces on her; STYLE_FIT 0.93 and the step up to 1m6½f from a career best of 1m2f are both meaningful doubts.|

runners_data.name: Prizeland
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up filly who won on soft at 1m2f and has placed consistently, with Oisin Murphy aboard; the step to 1m6½f is unproven and the controlled pace from Fairy Glen may not generate sufficient late momentum, but her reliable finishing pattern and class make her the most credible of the hold-up types if conditions suit closers.|

races.paceDynamic: Fairy Glen is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will dictate a solo, uncontested gallop over 1m6½f on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster. The pace will be sustainable rather than scorching — a lone leader able to control tempo on soft ground at this trip is a powerful tactical advantage, particularly on a flat, sweeping track that suits those who travel comfortably in front and avoid the kick-for-home scrummage. Behind her, Consent, Danielle, and Waardah are the natural prominent types who will track the leader in the first rank, while Floresta and Prizeland are genuine hold-up fillies who will need cover and a strong enough gallop to generate a meaningful late run. The field contains more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate: Nyra, Cameo, and Ryka are all natural prominent/front-side horses mapped to midfield because Fairy Glen, Consent, Danielle, and Waardah are likeliest to actually secure those forward positions, leaving the redistributed trio in a less natural role. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel efficiently close to a controlled pace and quicken from a forward position — prominent trackers with soft-ground class are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fairy Glen controls, trackers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Fairy Glen sets a measured, uncontested lead and the race is run at a steady-to-moderate tempo that keeps the field bunched and travelling well.
scenarios.body: Fairy Glen's uncontested lead allows her to set every fraction on her own terms, conserving energy through soft ground, but her long absence (112 days) and STYLE_FIT flag mean a prominent tracker timing a late challenge is the likeliest winner; Consent, Danielle, and Waardah — all proven at the trip or going and positioned just off the pace — are ideally placed to pounce in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft ground grinds out stayers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely testing on the soft surface and the race becomes a stamina-sapping slog that exposes class and conditioning over raw speed.
scenarios.body: A strong, relentless gallop on soft ground at 1m6½f filters out any filly with stamina questions and rewards those whose form profiles scream staying ability and soft-ground affinity; Consent's sim-going record (5/8 runs) and Waardah's three wins on similar ground in her last eight runs make both highly relevant here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up fillies finish strongly
scenarios.trigger: If Fairy Glen's controlled pace is brisk enough to string the field out and create genuine late momentum for those held up.
scenarios.body: Floresta and Prizeland have genuine hold-up profiles and enough class to produce a sustained late run if the gallop is sufficient to gap the field and leave a opening in the straight; Prizeland in particular has won on soft and shown a reliable finishing kick at both 1m2f and 1m4f, but she has not been tested at this trip, which is a genuine query.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed types disrupt race shape
scenarios.trigger: If Nyra, Cameo, or Ryka aggressively push for prominence and force a faster, contested early gallop that scrambles the expected order.
scenarios.body: Should any of the redistributed prominent types refuse to settle back and instead press Fairy Glen for the lead, the pace dynamic changes materially and could suit a closer who has been dragged into the race from behind; however, none of Nyra, Cameo, or Ryka have the STYLE_FIT credentials to be confident they improve by doing so, and Cameo's recent form string is ragged.

watchPoints.text: Fairy Glen's 112-day layoff is the race's biggest variable — watch in the paddock and early in the race for signs of fitness; if she fades turning for home after setting the pace, the race opens up for Danielle and Waardah who are tracking just behind.|

Cameo, Nyra, and Ryka are all natural prominent horses who have been pushed to midfield by the race shape — watch the early exchanges to see if any of them push forward aggressively, which would compress the pace and materially change the tempo for everyone.|

Waardah has strong soft-ground form (three wins on sim-going) and wears headgear that has coincided with her best performances — if she settles into a forward position tracking Fairy Glen without being crowded out, she could be travelling dangerously well at the furlong pole.|

Prizeland's Oisin Murphy booking is notable given the trainer's 14-day strike rate (12/60) — watch whether Murphy attempts to make ground earlier than the filly's hold-up profile suggests, which could signal the team expects the pace to be insufficient for a straight late charge.|

races.name: Betfred May Hill Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Ballyskeagh
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits this strongly-run mile perfectly; Joseph O'Brien's filly ran 2nd over 8f on Good and has the profile of a horse who will relish the test of stamina as rivals tire late, and 12 days since last run looks fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Beguiled
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden have this lightly-raced filly entering Group company off just two starts; prominent style and a win at 7f on Good are solid credentials but she steps sharply up in class and the soft-ish ground is an unknown factor.

runners_data.name: Eabha
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's consistent filly has placed twice on soft ground and won on Good, giving her the broadest going profile in the field; prominent style over 7f puts her on the premises, and the step to 8f on Good To Soft looks likely to suit her stamina.

runners_data.name: Martinet
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's lead horse drops back from 7f form and will push forward from the off; the concern is that with multiple rivals equally determined to lead, Martinet may be outpaced or find the front too crowded, and a 33-day absence is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Musical Times
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby and William Buick's unbeaten filly is the class reference in the race; she will lead or race very prominently, and whether she can sustain a strong gallop on Good To Soft over 1m against proven stamina types is the critical question — the ground is untested territory.

runners_data.name: Scommessa Sicura
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly has been placed in five consecutive runs and will attempt to lead again under Oisin Murphy; her one soft-ground run produced a 2nd place but she has yet to win, and being pushed into a pace battle by multiple rivals on this occasion may cost her late.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Rain
runners_data.note: Jim Bolger's filly arrives on the back of an 8f win on Good and has a consistent record over a mile; prominent style, proven stamina, and Rossa Ryan in the saddle make her an obvious fit for a strongly-run race where stayers are rewarded.

runners_data.name: Speckles
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien's filly has a modest recent form string of 6-2-5 but the Ballydoyle team rarely run 2yo fillies in Group 2 company without purpose; prominent style could see her travel into contention, but her form figures give limited confidence.

runners_data.name: Tall Trees
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's filly won her maiden last time over 7f on Good and will press forward again under Tom Marquand; she faces a significant class jump into Group 2 company and the step to 8f on soft ground may expose the limits of her stamina if the pace is truly hot.

runners_data.name: Thuritha
runners_data.note: David Simcock's hold-up filly won over 8f at Salisbury (Standard, AW) and has placed on soft ground previously; the hold-up style is perfectly suited to this pace scenario but her OR of 80 is well below the leading protagonists and she needs a significant improvement to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Tie A Navyribbon
runners_data.note: William Stone's charge won over 8f on Good and will race prominently; with a T14 of 0/1 and stepping into Group 2 company from a far more modest level, she is likely to be outclassed once the race quickens, though she could briefly feature up front before fading.

races.paceDynamic: Four genuine front-runners — Scommessa Sicura, Musical Times, Tall Trees, and Martinet — are set to contest the early lead on Good To Soft ground at Doncaster's straight mile, with Tie A Navyribbon also likely to push forward, creating a strongly-run race from the outset. The pace is not merely probable but near-certain given the profile and ambitions of these runners, meaning the field will be strung out early and the stamina demands of soft-ish ground will bite hard in the final two furlongs. Musical Times (William Buick, Charlie Appleby) may ultimately dictate the terms from the front if she asserts class, while Scommessa Sicura and Tall Trees will press aggressively, preventing any single horse from stealing an uncontested lead. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with proven stamina and soft-ground form — in particular hold-up and patient prominent types who can travel efficiently and pounce late as the pace-setters empty, making Ballyskeagh, Sea Of Rain, and Eabha the profiles best aligned to the likely finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other off through a genuine gallop, the hold-up and patient prominent horses land on empty rivals.
scenarios.body: With four runners fighting for supremacy, the pace collapses the stamina of the pace-setters in the final furlong on softening ground, leaving the closers with a clear path; Ballyskeagh and Sea Of Rain, both proven over 8f and comfortable on soft, are ideally suited to this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Horse Leads and Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Times asserts dominance from the front, controls a strong but measured tempo, and has enough class to see it out on the ground.
scenarios.body: Buick on Musical Times for Appleby is a formidable combination, and if she dictates without being pestered into a suicidal pace she can convert raw class into a front-running victory; her unbeaten record and Group 2 context make this a credible alternative shape if rivals fade earlier than expected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops at a strong but sustainable pace and a prominently-placed horse travels comfortably before quickening to hold off late challengers.
scenarios.body: Eabha's consistent form, soft-ground experience, and prominent racing style place her well to exploit a scenario where the race is run at a tempo that suits a well-positioned filly; Sea Of Rain's recent 1m win on Good ground and prominent style also fits this profile strongly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners uncharacteristically settle and the pace proves slower than expected, allowing one of the pace-setters to steal a march.
scenarios.body: Doncaster's straight mile on soft ground can occasionally produce false tempos if runners check and settle, and a horse like Tall Trees, who took her maiden well, could potentially benefit from an easy lead; this scenario is the least likely given the sheer number of confirmed front-runners who will inevitably push each other.

watchPoints.text: Musical Times and Scommessa Sicura are both natural front-runners under top jockeys — watch for a pace war between them in the opening quarter-mile that could fatally compromise both their chances.

Eabha's soft-ground form (two placings on Soft, one win on Good) makes her a horse to monitor closely during the race — if she travels strongly into the final 2f she becomes a serious threat in this scenario.

Sea Of Rain has shown stamina over 8f twice this season and Jim Bolger's runners often improve on a sounder surface — watch whether she is travelling easily into the straight, as she may hit the line stronger than her market position suggests.
Ballyskeagh is drawn to be covered up and produced late by J M Sheridan — track where she is positioned at the 3f pole, as Joseph O'Brien's horses often need a clean run to deliver their best effort.

The going report consistently returns Good To Soft across the card despite the 'Soft' classification in the race header — if the ground is firmer than feared, Musical Times' untested soft-ground profile becomes less of a concern.

races.name: Meadowhall X Flannels Beauty Bar Nursery Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Al Wathba
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's promising colt has already won over 8f at Sandown and placed twice over 7f on Good, so this mile on Good to Soft looks ideal; William Buick's positional intelligence from a prominent berth could prove decisive in a pace-collapse scenario.

runners_data.name: Waasil
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke fires well at a 12/40 14-day strike rate and Waasil arrives having won twice including over 8f on Good ground, making him the most experienced front-runner in the field; 49 days off is worth monitoring but Burke horses rarely need the run.

runners_data.name: Zarakova
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly won over this exact trip on Good ground last time and Oisin Murphy gives her a significant jockey upgrade; her style means she needs to lead cleanly, and with Waasil and Keep Grating also wanting the front, she may be forced to burn fuel early to assert.

runners_data.name: Metamouse
runners_data.note: Won on Soft ground and has placed twice on similar surfaces, giving her the most compelling soft-ground profile in the field; she races prominently and David Loughnane's team has a quiet 14-day record (0/20) so a small flag on stable form, but her stamina and going credentials are real assets.

runners_data.name: Keep Grating
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's colt has been progressive, winning last time over 7f on Good, but stepping up to a mile in a three-way pace battle on Good to Soft looks a significant ask; most likely to be the front-runner squeezed out of a clean lead, which would compromise his entire race.

runners_data.name: Primal
runners_data.note: Races naturally as a prominent type but has been mapped to the rear given the pace-heavy field — his actual style means he is unlikely to get a genuine hold-up run; his recent form string (64842) is modest and the 15 days since last run is not a concern, but his chance is conditional on everything going wrong for those ahead.

races.paceDynamic: Waasil, Zarakova, and Keep Grating are all confirmed front-runners in a six-runner field, meaning the pace battle begins immediately from the stalls and a strong, relentless gallop over Doncaster's flat mile on Good to Soft ground is virtually guaranteed. These three will press each other hard through the early and middle portions of the race, burning significant energy and testing stamina — a crucial factor for two-year-olds stepping up or staying at a mile in testing conditions. With three pace-committed horses unable to all hold their natural position uncontested, the most likely outcome is a contested lead that plays directly into the hands of prominent-to-patient types who can track the carnage and pounce late. The field holds more front-running types than can comfortably lead, and among the lead trio, Waasil — most experienced at the mile and trained by Burke who fires well fresh — and Zarakova, with Oisin Murphy in the saddle, are best placed to actually control the gallop; Keep Grating is most likely to be shuffled back or forced wide. This race shape emphatically favours prominent racers with stamina and any horse possessing a genuine staying kick in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stayers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way lead battle burns out the front-runners and the race is run at a true stamina-sapping gallop from the off.
scenarios.body: Waasil, Zarakova, and Keep Grating fight each other into submission through the final two furlongs on softening ground, leaving the patient prominent horses to come through and mop up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Waasil or Zarakova — breaks quickly and establishes a clear lead before the others can match strides.
scenarios.body: The early pace is strong but measured enough for one horse to dictate comfortably on their own terms, conserving enough to hold on as stamina comes into play late on Good to Soft ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Tracks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest and consistent but not catastrophically fast, allowing a prominent horse to travel smoothly just off the lead and assert in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Al Wathba, well-suited to this trip having won at 8f already and trained by Appleby with Buick aboard, can track the battle at a comfortable distance and inherit the race late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that even prominent horses are compromised and a horse from further back gets a clear run home in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Primal, though a natural prominent racer repositioned at the rear due to the pace-heavy field, would need things to fall perfectly and rivals to be collectively spent for this to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Waasil, Zarakova, and Keep Grating — monitor which of the three front-runners actually breaks fastest from the stalls, as the one who leads cleanly will save crucial energy while the others burn into each other.

Zarakova's challenge depends heavily on whether Oisin Murphy can secure a clean lead without being pressed by Waasil immediately; if she is hassled from the first furlong, her chance diminishes sharply on stamina grounds.

Metamouse's soft-ground form is the strongest in the field — if the ground rides genuinely testing rather than easy Good to Soft as described, she becomes markedly more interesting and the gaps between runners could widen significantly.

Al Wathba's 15-day turnaround under William Buick for Appleby is worth noting — Appleby/Buick combinations at this track tend to have horses ready to perform first time out of a short break, and he is already proven at the mile.

Primal's redistribution to the rear of the field should not be taken at face value — he will likely race closer to the pace than his mapped position suggests, meaning the field is even more pace-heavy in the first half of the race than the chart implies.

races.name: East Midlands Airport And JET2 Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Kach Above
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at this trip at Doncaster give her a strong course-and-distance profile; front-running style suits a race she can control, though four rivals sharing that intent raises the risk of a pace war that exposes her on soft ground over the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Undiscovered
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's stable is in excellent form (T14: 9/48) and this horse owns a win on soft ground, the only horse bar Midgham Man in the field who has actually won in similar conditions; prominent style under Rossa Ryan means she can travel smoothly without being drawn into the pace battle.

runners_data.name: Rafe's Da Man
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over for Richard Hannon and that pairing alone demands respect; won his last start over this trip on Good and consistently runs prominently, making him ideally placed to pick off tiring leaders from two out.

runners_data.name: Weekend Roar
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer runner who finished 15th on soft last time out — that soft-ground form is a significant concern before any positives are weighed; prominent style means he needs to be sharper from the gate this time to get a useful position.

runners_data.name: Fuel The Jet
runners_data.note: Has a win over this course and trip but his last two outings have been disappointing, including a ninth in the most recent; front-running approach puts him right in the thick of the pace war, and on soft ground that could be punishing given his recent form trajectory.

runners_data.name: Midgham Man
runners_data.note: Won on soft ground over seven furlongs in his last start and is the most relevant soft-ground front-runner in the field on current evidence; drawn into a battle for the lead with Kach Above, his freshness (only 12 days since last run) and conditions form make him the most credible of the front-running group.

runners_data.name: Storm Blade
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's runner carries Oisin Murphy, the standout jockey booking in the field, which immediately elevates interest; his natural style sits between midfield and prominent, meaning he can travel off the hot pace without burning fuel, and his second last time out over this trip gives him solid placed form to build on.

runners_data.name: Love Rome
runners_data.note: Consistent placer in three recent runs but has not won; front-running tendencies backed by headgear (p) suggest connections are trying to galvanise her, though being embroiled in a four-way scramble for the lead on soft ground is not the recipe for a first win.

runners_data.name: Sanbona Warrior
runners_data.note: Won over this course and trip earlier in the season and has placed prominently since; headgear listed and prominent style mean William Knight is trying to keep him sharp, and on soft ground his stamina profile over seven furlongs is a genuine asset in a pace-dominated race.

races.paceDynamic: Kach Above, Fuel The Jet, and Midgham Man all want to lead, with Love Rome also likely to press forward, guaranteeing a strong gallop on Good to Soft ground over Doncaster's straight seven furlongs. Four horses contesting the same territory in the opening stages creates significant congestion, and with none likely to yield willingly, the pace will be genuine from flag to fall — stamina and resolution in the final two furlongs will be the decisive factors. Storm Blade has been redistributed to the rear on the map as a reflection of field balance, but this field is overloaded with pace-committed types, and among the front-runners it is Kach Above (highest-rated at OR 94 with back-to-back wins) and Midgham Man (sole soft-ground winner in the field) who are most likely to actually secure their positions. This strong-pace scenario squarely favours hold-up horses and those prominent types with proven stamina resolution — runners who can travel comfortably through the contest and unleash a sustained finish after the pace burns itself out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way battle for the lead produces a truly honest gallop that drains the front-runners in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Kach Above, Fuel The Jet, and Midgham Man pull each other along at a fierce tempo, leaving them vulnerable late as the soft ground compounds their effort; horses who travel smoothly off the pace and finish strongly through the final two furlongs are ideally positioned to benefit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Kach Above breaks sharply, establishes a comfortable lead, and controls the tempo to deny rivals a true killing gallop.
scenarios.body: Kach Above, the highest-rated runner at OR 94 and a back-to-back seven-furlong winner at this track, uses class and tactical authority to dictate a manageable pace and conserve enough for the final furlong; Laura Pearson's experienced handling of this sort of front-running assignment would be key to making it stick on soft ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Wins Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves honest but not excessive, allowing a prominent traveller with class to slide into contention and assert.
scenarios.body: Rafe's Da Man or Undiscovered, both sitting just off the battle for the lead under top jockeys in Ryan Moore and Rossa Ryan, travel economically and pick off the tiring pace-setters with authority from two furlongs out; Rafe's Da Man's recent winning form and Undiscovered's soft-ground win make both credible beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Muddled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If chaotic early jostling causes interference or a stumble in the front rank, disrupting the race shape entirely and flattening the gallop.
scenarios.body: A messy scenario in which pace horses lose their rhythm and the race becomes a scramble from midfield, opening the door for lower-rated runners with fresh legs; Love Rome and Sanbona Warrior, both placed in their recent runs, could sneak into a compressed finish.

watchPoints.text: Kach Above, Fuel The Jet, and Midgham Man — three confirmed front-runners plus Love Rome contesting the same early position creates a high-risk scramble off the gates; a bump or interference in the first two furlongs could compromise multiple runners simultaneously.

Storm Blade — Oisin Murphy's presence on an unassuming OR 81 runner invites the question of whether Balding has this horse significantly ahead of his mark; monitor market movement closely before the off.

Midgham Man — only 12 days since his last run and returning quickly to race conditions; if the soft ground has taken more out of him than connections appreciate, a quick turnaround in a strongly-run race could see him fade sharply.

Weekend Roar — his soft-ground form (15th last time on soft) is the worst performance in the field under similar conditions; despite James Doyle in the saddle, the going could undermine him before tactical questions are even asked.

Undiscovered — with only three career runs, her relative inexperience is worth monitoring in a field where the pace will be fierce; if she handles the early noise and settles, her soft-ground win and trainer form make her a key player late.

races.name: Pertemps Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Mocking
runners_data.note: Decent soft-ground placed form (1st and 2nd on Soft at 10f) but has been well beaten in bigger fields lately; a natural hold-up horse whose 80-day absence adds a fitness question, and the crowded rear means it will likely end up in midfield rather than its preferred backmarker slot.

runners_data.name: Devil's Peak
runners_data.note: William Buick in the saddle for Gosden is an obvious angle, and the 19-day turnaround looks sharp after a recent run; sole soft-going start produced a 6th over 14f but remains lightly raced over this sort of trip with upside, and as a genuine hold-up horse it maps naturally to a prominent midfield position in this shape.

runners_data.name: Railwayview Lady
runners_data.note: A hold-up type whose recent form reads poorly (8th, 9th in June) with no wins in five starts; placed once on Good over 8f but this 74-day layoff and a record that includes a 16th over 12f on Heavy suggests soft ground at 1m4f is a step into the unknown, and the redistribution to midfield compounds an already awkward profile.

runners_data.name: Masterinthewoods
runners_data.note: Four consecutive placings at 12f on Good ground is a strong and consistent form profile, but all those runs came on faster surfaces and the step to Soft is an unknown quantity; as a genuine hold-up horse with solid stamina, it maps well in this shape if the ground proves manageable.

runners_data.name: My Ballyquinn
runners_data.note: Won twice over 11-14f on Good ground and placed at 12-14f, making the trip and ability look solid; however both runs since a break have come on Soft and returned a 12th and 2nd, suggesting soft ground is at worst workable, and Tudhope's 4/47 trainer strike-rate over 14 days is not alarming given the horse's form.

runners_data.name: Alfred Wincham
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will set a solo pace under Rossa Ryan; his two wins have come on Good and a Soft-equivalent surface, and his style-fit tag is relevant — if his uncontested lead becomes too comfortable he may prove hard to catch, but his OR of 80 may leave him vulnerable to better-handicapped rivals if they produce a late burst.

runners_data.name: Mr Freedom
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with solid staying credentials, including a win over 20f and placed efforts over 14f on Soft; races prominently and has soft-ground course form which makes him one of the more tractable profile fits for this type of controlled gallop, though his recent form (8th, 5th) suggests he is not at peak.

runners_data.name: Eniac
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Brian Ellison on a three-year-old with a 3rd over 12f on Tapeta and placed at 13f on Good; a natural hold-up type squeezed into midfield by the field's composition, its style-fit discount is real, though Moore's ability to find an early forward position could partially offset the redistribution.

runners_data.name: Brighton View
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Good and placed at 10f on Good showing course and distance-relevant form; a natural hold-up type reassigned forward on the map, and its style-fit discount reflects genuine uncertainty about whether it can produce its best from a more prominent position than it would ordinarily prefer.

runners_data.name: Itica
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's recent win on Soft over 11f for Andrew Balding (T14: 12/60 is strong) gives the form a positive spin; races prominently and maps naturally in this shape, with solid soft-ground evidence, though stepping up from 11f to 1m4f is the key question mark for this three-year-old.

races.paceDynamic: Alfred Wincham is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him, he is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good To Soft ground over 1m4f — a track configuration that rewards those who can settle and travel. Mr Freedom and Itica are the only other prominent-leaning horses, but neither is likely to challenge Alfred Wincham for the lead, meaning the pace is controlled rather than contested. The bulk of the field — Mocking, Devil's Peak, Railwayview Lady, Masterinthewoods, My Ballyquinn, Eniac, and Brighton View — are natural hold-up types, though several of those are redistributed to midfield on the map because too many genuine closers exist for the rear slots to accommodate them all; of those, Brighton View, Eniac, and Mocking are least likely to secure a true back-of-the-field position and will race closer than their natural style dictates. A controlled, single-horse gallop on soft ground over this trip strongly favours hold-up horses with a sustained late run, particularly those with proven soft-ground form and the engine to pick up off a steady tempo — the tactical verdict points clearly to genuine closers who can travel sweetly in midfield and produce a finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Closers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Alfred Wincham sets an uncontested, even gallop and the race sets up as a one-turn staying test that rewards horses who travel and finish.
scenarios.body: Alfred Wincham dictates a comfortable tempo with no challenger, compressing the field into a bunch before the home turn, and those with the strongest staying kick off the bridle win the argument in the closing stages. Genuine hold-up types with soft-ground form — Devil's Peak, My Ballyquinn, and Masterinthewoods — are ideally placed to exploit this shape, with their handlers likely to have them tracking the pace in midfield without over-committing early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Alfred Wincham's uncontested lead is sufficient and the slow tempo lulls the field into leaving him alone for too long.
scenarios.body: On a soft surface that rewards galloping types who don't get into trouble, Alfred Wincham could dictate every yard and simply never be headed, as the pack fails to launch a coordinated challenge in time. His two wins over 12f on Good ground suggest he handles cut, and the slow-burning pace could play to his stamina if rivals leave their challenges too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Outstay Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that prominent racers Mr Freedom or Itica secure a position just off Alfred Wincham and benefit from racing handily throughout.
scenarios.body: Mr Freedom has soft-ground and staying form (3rd over 14f on Soft), and Itica showed a win on Soft over 11f recently, both profiles that allow them to travel economically close to the pace and grind opponents down in the final two furlongs. In a slow-run race where the hold-up horses cannot generate enough momentum from the rear, racing prominently becomes a positional advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If runners tagged as redistributed — Brighton View, Eniac, or Mocking — manage to find an unusually wide or forward position and produce a telling late run.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires these horses to race significantly out of their natural role given the crowded nature of the hold-up group, and the style-fit discounts applied to all three make this the least reliable shape in the field. Brighton View does hold a course win at 12f on Good and Eniac has placed on Soft, but the structural mismatch between their natural style and the race shape makes this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Alfred Wincham sets the only pace — if Rossa Ryan is allowed to dictate unchallenged from the start, monitor how far clear he steals entering the home straight, as no rival is likely to apply pressure until it may be too late.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Brighton View, Eniac, Mocking) will all be seeking a wider or more forward pitch than their natural style demands — watch the first two furlongs for positional congestion as they jostle for midfield ground rather than settling at the rear.

Devil's Peak's only soft-ground start produced a distant 6th over 14f — if the ground is testing rather than merely soft, William Buick may need to ride him more conservatively than ideal, which could compromise his run from a hold-up position.

Masterinthewoods has been placed in four consecutive races at 12f on Good — this is its first start on Soft and its first run at 1m4f, so watch whether David Probert asks it to travel forward or settles it off the pace in anticipation of the extra two furlongs in testing conditions.

Itica's trainer Andrew Balding holds a strong 14-day strike-rate (12/60) and Murphy is booked — watch market moves, as this combination targeting a soft-ground 1m4f handicap with a horse that just won on Soft could indicate a yard that believes the step up in trip will unlock improvement.
